title: Review: a dashboard reader for a repo-root declaration, before it reaches a consumer layout
question: Review this change before it merges. List the defects you would block on, ordered by impact, each with the evidence in the code shown and how you would verify it without waiting for a consumer to hit it; then list what you checked and found sound. Do not rewrite the feature; say what must change.

rubric.decision: Block the merge on two defects that cannot show in this repo and one that CI would catch. (1) SELF_REPO climbs three directories from the module, which is the repo root only in the source layout; in a consumer the module sits one directory deeper, so it resolves to the consumer's scripts directory and readManifest can never find the declaration. (2) Even resolved correctly, .windowed-views.json is read by path at runtime, is not importable, and is in neither CORE_ASSETS list, so the sync never ships it and a consumer has nothing to read. The consequence of both is that every queue chip loses its delta in a consumer (the unreadable case suppresses all five queues, including the ones that are not windowed). (3) Adding an asset is two edits: the hand-maintained sync-inventory mirror must change in lock-step or its parity test fails. The existing repo-root helper that is correct in both layouts should replace the arithmetic.

keyPoints.text: Finds that SELF_REPO is a fixed three-up climb from scripts/lib/dashboard/, correct only in the source layout; the sync-path-map header shows the file lands at scripts/.claude-skills/lib/dashboard/ in a consumer, so the same arithmetic yields the consumer's scripts/ directory, not its root.

Finds that .windowed-views.json is read by path at runtime (readManifest uses fs, not import), appears in neither CORE_ASSETS list, and so is never copied; in a consumer it is absent regardless of how the path is computed. Uses the oss-call-policy.json comment as the in-repo precedent for exactly this fs-read blind spot.

Works out the user-visible consequence from the diff: an unreadable declaration yields windowed: "unknown" for every queue, which withholds previous for ALL of them, so even the non-windowed queues (Q3, debt, upstream) lose their trend in a consumer, and it fails quietly (a neutral chip with an explanatory string), not loudly.

Notes that an asset added to sync-to-repos.mjs CORE_ASSETS must also be added to the hand-maintained mirror in sync-inventory.mjs (its comments say "keep in lock-step"), otherwise the verifier and other consumers of the inventory have a blind spot.

Names why the author's tests and CI cannot show (1) and (2): they run in the source layout where the arithmetic is right and the file is present, so a reproduction needs a consumer-layout fixture (a synced copy or a path-mapped temp tree), and the verification suggested is exactly that, not more unit tests of readManifest.

Recommends the existing repo-root helper (findRepoRootFromScript) instead of new arithmetic, treating a null result as unreadable rather than absent, and a note that the sync may also refuse an unpinned tracked destination for the new file (line-ending pin).

traps.text: Reviews only the logic of the diff (windowed/comparable/previous, the neutral chip wording) and passes it as correct because the tests pass.
Flags style or hypothetical issues (naming, a missing JSDoc, the default parameter) as blocking while missing the layout and shipping defects.
Spots the path arithmetic but proposes fixing it with more ../ or process.cwd(), or leaves the declaration out of the sync and has the dashboard fall back to a hard-coded queue list.
Treats "unknown for every queue" as acceptable degradation without noticing it also silences queues that are not windowed.

controls.gold:
Block this on two defects that this repo cannot show, plus one that CI will.

First, `SELF_REPO` is three `..` up from `scripts/lib/dashboard/`, which is the repo root only in the source layout. The path map says `scripts/<rest>` lands at `scripts/.claude-skills/<rest>` in a consumer, so the module sits one level deeper and the same arithmetic yields `<consumer>/scripts`. `readManifest` then returns `missing`, and the collector maps that to `windowed: 'unknown'`.

Second, even with the path right, `.windowed-views.json` is read by `fs` and never imported, and it is in neither `CORE_ASSETS` list. The import walk cannot see it, so the sync does not ship it; the `oss-call-policy.json` comment records exactly this blind spot and its cost. In a consumer the file is absent.

Consequence: in every consumer the declaration is unreadable, `unknown` withholds `previous` for all queues, and the chips that are not windowed lose their trend as well, quietly, as neutral chips with an explanation. Nothing fails.

Third, `sync-inventory.mjs` keeps a hand mirror of `CORE_ASSETS` ("keep in lock-step"); adding the asset to one list only breaks the parity test and leaves the verifier blind to it.

Tests and CI run in the source layout, so verify with a consumer-layout fixture: a path-mapped temp tree, or an actual `sync` dry run. Replace the arithmetic with `findRepoRootFromScript` (correct in both layouts), treat null as unreadable, add the file to both lists, and expect the line-ending pin check to ask for a glob.

## Decision

Do not merge as is: fix the root resolution, ship the declaration through both asset lists, and add a consumer-layout test.
controls.trap:
The change is sound and can merge. The logic is easy to follow: `collectQueues` reads the declaration once, derives a three-valued `windowed` (yes, no, unknown), and uses it to decide whether to attach `previous`. The safe default is the right one, since an unreadable declaration suppresses every trend rather than claiming one, and the chip text says why. The measured incident in the comments (0 shared rows, 110 of 116 still open) justifies the behaviour change, and the new tests exercise all three states, including the unreadable path.

Two small things. The new `manifestRoot` option has a default that is evaluated at module load; that is fine, but a one-line JSDoc on `SELF_REPO` would help. And the neutral-chip detail strings are long for a chip, so consider trimming them. Neither blocks.

The `SELF_REPO` computation is the same three-level climb other dashboard modules use to find the repo root, and it matches the layout of this repository, where `scripts/lib/dashboard` is three directories below the root. It is covered by the tests that read the real `.windowed-views.json`, and CI is green.

Consumers will pick this up through the normal sync, so no extra wiring is needed; the dashboard module and its imports are already in the sync closure, and `windowed-views.mjs` comes along as an import of the collector.

## Decision

Approve and merge; address the JSDoc and the chip wording in a follow-up.
